name: Japanese Carmine
lede: Japanese Carmine is a vivid, slightly brownish red, close kin to the dye word carmine, and the English name under which ColorHub files the Japanese color enji-iro.

sections.title: Carmine, and its Japanese name
sections.body:
The 1955 ISCC-NBS system would call this swatch's family a vivid red, its Munsell notation reading 5.4R 3.6/10.3 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[orient-red]], [[purple-madder]] and [[rouge]], at 3.7, 
ColorHub's library pairs it with a traditional Japanese name, enji-iro (臙脂色), meaning cochineal red or rouge, the same dye tradition under a different, older naming system [2]. The closest core app color is [[carmine]], about six units away, and the library also notes a near-duplicate it calls Crimson (UA), under two and a half units off [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this red in 102 of 23,781 paintings, a little over four tenths of one per cent [3]. The earliest match is a 1260 Green Tara thangka, centuries before any dated record of this color name, so that is a lookalike hue and not a pigment record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. The 1400s show the strongest lift, at more than four times the overall baseline [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings and thangkas, and a match says nothing about whether cochineal or any other dye was actually used [3].
